questions.question:
Identify the sentence with correct inversion after a negative adverbial phrase.

A) Never have I seen such a beautiful sunset.
B) Rarely I have seen such a beautiful sunset.
C) Only once have I visited Paris.
D) Since childhood, he has been interested in music.
options: Never have I seen such a beautiful sunset.
Rarely I have seen such a beautiful sunset.
Only once have I visited Paris.
Since childhood, he has been interested in music.
questions.answer: Only once have I visited Paris.

questions.question:
Which sentence correctly uses a cleft sentence to emphasize the location?

A) It was in London that they first met.
B) It was London where they first met.
C) London was where they first met.
D) They first met in London is where it happened.
options: It was in London that they first met.
It was London where they first met.
London was where they first met.
They first met in London is where it happened.
questions.answer: It was in London that they first met.

questions.question:
Select the correct form of the third conditional to express a hypothetical situation in the past that did not happen.

A) If I had known about the meeting, I would have attended.
B) If I had known about the meeting, I would have attended.
C) If I had known about the meeting, I would have attended.
D) If I had known about the meeting, I would have attended.
options: If I had known about the meeting, I would have attended.
If I had known about the meeting, I would have attended.
If I had known about the meeting, I would have attended.
If I had known about the meeting, I would have attended.
questions.answer: If I had known about the meeting, I would have attended.

questions.question:
Which sentence correctly uses the subjunctive mood after 'wish' to express a desire contrary to fact?

A) I wish it was raining now.
B) I wish it were raining now.
C) I wish it be raining now.
D) I wish it is raining now.
options: I wish it was raining now.
I wish it were raining now.
I wish it be raining now.
I wish it is raining now.
questions.answer: I wish it were raining now.

questions.question:
Identify the sentence with correct ellipsis where the word 'they' is omitted appropriately.

A) John likes coffee and tea, but Mary prefers tea and not coffee.
B) John likes coffee and tea, but Mary prefers tea and coffee not.
C) John likes coffee and tea, but Mary prefers tea and not coffee.
D) John likes coffee and tea, but Mary prefers tea and coffee not.
options: John likes coffee and tea, but Mary prefers tea and not coffee.
John likes coffee and tea, but Mary prefers tea and coffee not.
John likes coffee and tea, but Mary prefers tea and not coffee.
John likes coffee and tea, but Mary prefers tea and coffee not.
questions.answer: John likes coffee and tea, but Mary prefers tea and not coffee.
